summary: I sent the exact message once. Claude looked around the repo (ls, git status, Read index.html), then edited index.html directly to add a checkbox inside a label: `<label><input type="checkbox" id="task-done"> Done</label>`. It took about 17 seconds. It didn't brainstorm, didn't ask me anything, and didn't ask permission first.
reasoning: Both criteria pass. Claude saw the request as mechanical and made the edit straight away, and the page now has an `<input type="checkbox">`. The session log shows no Skill call of any kind, and Claude didn't ask for a go-ahead or raise a consequence before editing.

observations.description: After finishing, Claude noted a scope point: the page has no task list, so this is one standalone checkbox, and repeating it per task or saving its state would be a bigger change. It said this after the edit, not as a question before it, so it didn't block anything. It was useful context.
Before the edit, Claude said "rung 2 of the skill ladder". That is plugin jargon a normal user wouldn't understand; saying it would just make the change directly would be clearer.

On first launch there were four setup screens: theme, security notes, folder trust and the bypass-permissions warning. On both the trust screen and the bypass warning, the highlighted default is "No, exit", so I had to press Down before Enter each time. This is normal first-run behaviour, but it adds friction to automated runs.

The last assistant turn used about 34k cache-read input tokens, 505 cache-creation tokens and 139 output tokens. The earlier turn had 353 output tokens, 96 of them thinking. I couldn't find coding-agent-token-usage.json in the run directory while testing; it's probably generated after the run.

criteria.criterion: The agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log shows the assistant's tool calls in this order: Bash (ls), Bash (git status/log), Read index.html, then Edit. Before the edit Claude wrote: "This is a basic form control with one obvious implementation — rung 2 of the skill ladder, so I'm making the edit directly rather than brainstorming." index.html on disk now contains `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">`.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming Skill invocation, and no go-ahead request or stated consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: Counting tool_use names in the session JSONL with jq ('.message.content[] | select(.type=="tool_use") | .name' | sort | uniq -c) returned only: 2 Bash, 1 Edit, 1 Read. There was no Skill call. The only text before the edit is the one-line explanation quoted above, with no question and no consequence. I never had to send a second message.
